subject: Duplicate metering charge during April migration window + VAT handling
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@clearshore.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: finance@clearshore.com
Date: 2027-04-07T08:12:00+01:00
Subject: Unexpected duplicate charge on April 1 invoice (attached)

Hi Connor / Ben,

Hope you’re well. We reconciled our April billing and noticed the line for 2027-04-01 appears to have been billed twice — the usage spike that day was duplicated in both the standard meter and the migration-metering bucket. I’ve attached the invoice and our internal usage CSV for the window.

Impact: we see a gross overcharge of €12,450 on invoice 20270401 (invoice.pdf attached). Clearshore is an EU-registered company and we need the credit to reflect the proper VAT treatment (we are reverse-charging under our VAT ID).

Request: please confirm you will issue a credit memo for the duplicate usage and reissue an adjusted invoice or provide a formal credit memo we can apply against the outstanding amount. Also include the VAT breakdown (gross credit and VAT note) so our AP team can process it.

We’d like confirmation by EOD tomorrow if possible — we have month-end close next week.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Finance
Clearshore Logistics
(elena.rossi@clearshore.com)

Attachments: invoice_20270401.pdf, usage_report_apr.csv

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: elena.rossi@clearshore.com
Date: 2027-04-07T10:05:00+01:00
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected duplicate charge on April 1 invoice (attached)

Team — forwarding Clearshore’s note. Quick summary: duplicate metering during migration window created a ~€12.45k gross overcharge on invoice 20270401. They require a credit memo showing gross amount and VAT treatment to allow reverse-charge processing.

Marissa — can you confirm the correct credit mechanics (goodwill vs corrective credit), whether we need to reissue the invoice or just issue a credit memo, and the expected timeline?

David — please advise on VAT treatment for cross-border B2B reverse-charge here; Clearshore say they’ll provide VAT ID. If we mark as reverse-charge, what language needs to appear on the credit memo/invoice?

Ben — looping you in for commercial sign-off if we need to treat as goodwill vs corrective accounting entry.

Connor

--Forwarded attachments: invoice_20270401.pdf, usage_report_apr.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: elena.rossi@clearshore.com
Date: 2027-04-08T09:24:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected duplicate charge on April 1 invoice (attached)

Thanks for the ping — reviewed the usage CSV and our billing logs. Confirming:

- Cause: migration job re-ingested a delta and duplicated a subset of hourly aggregates for 2027-04-01; duplicate rows were included in the metering pipeline for that date only.
- Amount: duplicate tokens = €12,450 gross (currency EUR).
- Accounting treatment: we recommend issuing a corrective credit memo (not a goodwill concession) because this was an overbill error; this preserves clean ledgers for both parties.

Proposed steps (timeline in parentheses):
1) Issue a two-line credit memo referencing invoice 20270401:
   - Line 1: Credit — Duplicate usage (gross) €12,450 (immediate)
   - Line 2: VAT note — reverse charge (0% VAT on the credit) with supplier and buyer VAT IDs noted (immediate)
2) Reissue adjusted invoice if Clearshore prefers a netted document for AP (optional; 48 hrs)
3) Push credit memo to Clearshore and CC accounting for remittance (immediate)

I’ve prepared a draft credit memo (credit_memo_draft.pdf) with suggested language: "Reverse charge — VAT to be accounted for by recipient under Article 196 (B2B intra-EU supply)" and a reference to Clearshore’s invoice and our internal billing ticket. If we proceed with corrective credit, we need Elena to confirm Clearshore’s VAT registration number to include on the credit memo.

David, please confirm the reverse-charge wording is sufficient for our EU filings.

Ben, please confirm commercial sign-off — this is an operational billing error; we are not proposing an extra goodwill concession beyond the corrective credit.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Billing Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachments: credit_memo_draft.pdf

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@clearshore.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: finance@clearshore.com, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-09T16:37:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Duplicate charge on April 1 invoice + VAT handling — VAT ID attached

Hi Marissa / Connor,

Thanks — that plan works for us. Our VAT details below for inclusion on the credit memo:
VAT ID: IT12345678901
Company legal name: Clearshore Logistics S.p.A.
Registered address: Via Marina 18, Trieste, Italy

We accept the corrective credit treatment (not goodwill). We also prefer the credit memo as a standalone document (we will net it against the open invoice on our side). If you can send the signed PDF, our AP team will process within 5 business days.

Two small asks:
- please include the following line on the memo: "Reverse charge — VAT to be accounted for by the recipient (Article 196) — VAT ID IT12345678901"
- include the original invoice reference (20270401) and your internal billing ticket number (RB-20270401-07) so our ERPs match.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — let us know ETA for the credit memo pdf.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Finance
Clearshore Logistics
(elena.rossi@clearshore.com)
